top_event.headline: Bessemer Steel Industrial Dominance
top_event.wealth_driver: Carnegie Steel dominates transatlantic steelmaking through vertical integration of iron ore, coal, and coke logistics.

top_event.headline: The $480M U.S. Steel Buyout
top_event.wealth_driver: Carnegie sells Carnegie Steel to J.P. Morgan for $480 million in gold-backed bonds, setting the highest private fortune of the early industrial era.

top_event.headline: Inception of the Carnegie Philanthropies
top_event.wealth_driver: Carnegie begins liquidating his U.S. Steel bond portfolio into public trusts, while Standard Oil expands global kerosene distributions.

top_event.headline: Standard Oil Closes the Valuation Gap
top_event.wealth_driver: Pipeline monopoly margins and railroad rebates expand Rockefeller's unencumbered equity toward Carnegie's remaining bond holdings.

top_event.headline: Global Kerosene Logistics Reach
top_event.wealth_driver: Rapid worldwide consumer demand for lighting fuel accelerates Standard Oil net profits across European and Asian export lines.

top_event.headline: Rockefeller Overtakes Carnegie
top_event.wealth_driver: Expanding gasoline consumption from early automobile manufacturing pushes Standard Oil earnings above Carnegie's philanthropic endowment.

top_event.headline: Sherman Act Prosecution Begins
top_event.wealth_driver: The U.S. government files antitrust proceedings against Standard Oil while record dividend payouts drive Rockefeller's net worth higher.

top_event.headline: The Panic of 1907
top_event.wealth_driver: As Wall Street banks face severe liquidity runs, Rockefeller and Morgan intervene with private capital reserves, acquiring discounted industrial shares.

top_event.headline: Model T Debut & Fuel Expansion
top_event.wealth_driver: Henry Ford's introduction of the Model T establishes assembly-line mass production, securing long-term gasoline consumption and lifting Standard Oil cash flows.

top_event.headline: Standard Oil Trust Peak Valuation
top_event.wealth_driver: Standard Oil reaches the height of its trust valuation ahead of antitrust dissolution, lifting Rockefeller's fortune to $700M nominal ($26.24B CPI-adjusted).

top_event.headline: Standard Oil Trust Peak
top_event.wealth_driver: Near-monopoly control of domestic and export petroleum refining pushes Rockefeller's fortune to $800 million nominal ($28.77 billion CPI-adjusted).

top_event.headline: Supreme Court Orders Standard Oil Breakup
top_event.wealth_driver: The U.S. Supreme Court mandates the dissolution of Standard Oil into 34 independent operating companies, initiating a sharp valuation expansion for shareholders.

top_event.headline: Standard Oil Spin-Off Equity Revaluation
top_event.wealth_driver: Public trading of shares in Standard Oil of New Jersey, Standard Oil of California, and Socony surges, widening Rockefeller's lead over industrial peers.

top_event.headline: Highland Park Moving Assembly Line Debut
top_event.wealth_driver: Henry Ford institutes the moving assembly line for Model T production, slashing assembly time per vehicle from 12 hours to 93 minutes.

top_event.headline: Outbreak of World War I
top_event.wealth_driver: European wartime demand escalates heavy industrial orders for Krupp artillery and Du Pont chemicals, while Ford introduces the historic $5 workday.

top_event.headline: Allied Defense Procurement Surge
top_event.wealth_driver: British and French contracts for American smokeless gunpowder, transport vehicles, and refined fuel accelerate profits across U.S. manufacturing.

top_event.headline: First Nominal Billionaire Landmark
top_event.wealth_driver: Combined equity in Standard Oil spin-offs crosses $1.05 billion nominal ($32.28 billion CPI-adjusted), officially establishing Rockefeller as history's first nominal billionaire.

top_event.headline: U.S. Enters World War I & Wartime Price Inflation
top_event.wealth_driver: War mobilization accelerates petroleum, aluminum, and chemical revenues, while consumer price inflation jumps by 17.8%.

top_event.headline: Armistice & Ford Industrial Expansion
top_event.wealth_driver: As hostilities conclude, Du Pont transitions toward civilian plastics and automotive coatings, while Henry Ford prepares for the postwar car boom.

top_event.headline: Ford Minority Shareholder Buyout & Carnegie's Passing
top_event.wealth_driver: Henry Ford executes a $105 million buyout of all minority shares to secure 100% private ownership of Ford Motor Company, while Andrew Carnegie passes away.

top_event.headline: Post-WWI Commodity Rebound
top_event.wealth_driver: Rapid adoption of consumer automobiles and factory fuel demand lifts Standard Oil spin-off market values, keeping Rockefeller at the peak of private global wealth.

top_event.headline: Post-War Deflation Resilience
top_event.wealth_driver: Despite severe postwar industrial contraction and general price deflation, vast cash holdings and steady fuel sales protect Rockefeller's dominant balance sheet.

top_event.headline: Philanthropic Endowments & German Conglomerate Expansion
top_event.wealth_driver: Rockefeller accelerates equity distributions into foundation trusts, while Hugo Stinnes builds Central Europe's largest shipping, mining, and manufacturing cartel.

top_event.headline: Two Million Model Ts Annually
top_event.wealth_driver: Ford produces two million vehicles in a single year, rapidly narrowing the wealth gap with Rockefeller's endowment-reduced fortune.

top_event.headline: Henry Ford Captures Global #1
top_event.wealth_driver: River Rouge vertical integration and assembly-line throughput push Henry Ford past Rockefeller to become the world's richest private individual.

top_event.headline: River Rouge Peak Industrial Integration
top_event.wealth_driver: Sole ownership of blast furnaces, rail lines, timberlands, and glassmaking plants maximizes margins across Ford Motor Company's operations.

top_event.headline: Five-Day Workweek & Match Monopoly Expansion
top_event.wealth_driver: Ford establishes the 40-hour workweek, while Swedish financier Ivar Kreuger expands sovereign lending across Europe to secure state match monopolies.

top_event.headline: Model A Retooling Capital Expenditure
top_event.wealth_driver: Ford halts Model T production after 15 million units to retool for the Model A, absorbing massive capital expenditures entirely out of corporate liquid reserves.

top_event.headline: Commercial Success of the Model A
top_event.wealth_driver: Rapid consumer adoption of the Model A restores operating cash flows, while Ivar Kreuger issues hundreds of millions in debentures to acquire European match cartels.

top_event.headline: Wall Street Crash & Peak Automotive Fortune
top_event.wealth_driver: On the eve of the Great Crash, Ford's debt-free industrial empire reaches $1.30 billion nominal ($25.34 billion CPI-adjusted), while public equity markets collapse in October.

top_event.headline: Great Depression Onset & Liquid Balance Sheet Defense
top_event.wealth_driver: Despite global consumer auto demand contracting sharply, Ford Motor Company's zero-debt balance sheet and massive cash reserves protect Henry Ford's position at global #1.

top_event.headline: Industrial Retrenchment & Baker's Passing
top_event.wealth_driver: Ford slashes Model A output to preserve operating cash as deflation intensifies across global markets, while First National Bank titan George Fisher Baker passes away.

top_event.headline: Depression Trough & The Kreuger Crash
top_event.wealth_driver: Swedish match monopolist Ivar Kreuger collapses into bankruptcy and suicide, erasing his fortune, while Ford's retained earnings weather the worst year of industrial deflation.

top_event.headline: New Deal Banking Reforms & East Texas Oil Boom
top_event.wealth_driver: Emergency banking measures stabilize the monetary base, while H.L. Hunt aggressively amasses drilling rights across the prolific East Texas oil field.

top_event.headline: Gold Reserve Act & Heavy Industry Rebound
top_event.wealth_driver: The Gold Reserve Act devalues the dollar to $35/oz, stimulating commodity prices as German industrial procurement begins reviving Krupp steelworks.

top_event.headline: Flathead V8 Dominance & Hughes Tool Expansion
top_event.wealth_driver: Commercial success of the Ford Flathead V8 secures automotive profit margins, while Hughes Tool Company's patented drill bits capture over 75% of the global market.

top_event.headline: Ford Foundation Charter & European Rearmament
top_event.wealth_driver: Henry and Edsel Ford create the Ford Foundation using non-voting stock to shelter ownership from estate duties, while Krupp armaments production expands sharply.

top_event.headline: Passing of Rockefeller & Andrew Mellon
top_event.wealth_driver: John D. Rockefeller dies in May followed by Andrew W. Mellon in August; Henry Ford remains the lone multi-hundred-millionaire from the original industrial era.

top_event.headline: Arabian Petroleum Discovery & European Armament Mobilization
top_event.wealth_driver: Commercial oil is struck at Dammam No. 7 in Saudi Arabia, while Krupp's heavy artillery manufacturing reaches capacity under German state rearmament contracts.

top_event.headline: Outbreak of World War II in Europe
top_event.wealth_driver: The invasion of Poland sparks global conflict, prompting immediate defense contracts for Krupp armaments, Du Pont chemicals, and heavy vehicle producers.

top_event.headline: Arsenal of Democracy Planning
top_event.wealth_driver: As war engulfs Europe, Ford Motor Company begins retooling its automotive assembly lines for Allied defense materiel while preserving 100% private family equity.

top_event.headline: Willow Run Bomber Facility Groundbreaking
top_event.wealth_driver: Ford initiates construction of the mile-long Willow Run plant near Ypsilanti to apply automotive mass-production techniques to B-24 Liberator airframes.

top_event.headline: Total Industrial War Conversion
top_event.wealth_driver: Commercial passenger car assembly terminates entirely as Ford converts all production to military tanks, engines, and gliders under federal procurement programs.

top_event.headline: Passing of Edsel Ford & Lex Krupp Decree
top_event.wealth_driver: Edsel Ford dies in May, thrusting an 80-year-old Henry Ford back into company leadership, while the Lex Krupp decree preserves sole dynasty ownership for Alfried Krupp.

top_event.headline: Willow Run One-Hour Bomber Output
top_event.wealth_driver: Ford reaches its wartime production zenith, completing an entire four-engine B-24 bomber every 63 minutes at Willow Run.

top_event.headline: Henry Ford II Takes Reins & Krupp Confiscation
top_event.wealth_driver: Henry Ford II assumes the company presidency to initiate postwar modernization, while Allied occupation forces arrest Alfried Krupp and seize his Ruhr assets.

top_event.headline: Post-War Civilian Reconversion
top_event.wealth_driver: Passenger car assembly restarts amid heavy pent-up civilian consumer demand during Henry Ford's final full year of life.

top_event.headline: Passing of Henry Ford
top_event.wealth_driver: Henry Ford dies at age 83, dividing his stock among family heirs and the Ford Foundation; John D. Rockefeller Jr. reclaims global #1 private individual.

top_event.headline: Fortune Names H.L. Hunt Richest Operating Businessman
top_event.wealth_driver: Fortune's landmark wealth investigation highlights independent oil wildcatter H.L. Hunt pumping 65,000 barrels per day across Texas and Louisiana.

top_event.headline: Getty Acquired Saudi-Kuwaiti Neutral Zone Concession
top_event.wealth_driver: J. Paul Getty risks $9.5 million cash plus royalty commitments to obtain a 60-year exploration concession in the Saudi Neutral Zone, positioning for an oil boom.

top_event.headline: Post-War Asset Consolidation
top_event.wealth_driver: Extensive commercial holdings across Manhattan, including Rockefeller Center, alongside diversified Standard Oil equity maintain Rockefeller Jr. atop global private wealth.

top_event.headline: Restoration of Krupp Assets & Korean War Mobilization
top_event.wealth_driver: Allied authorities revoke confiscation orders against Alfried Krupp, while wartime defense logistics boost shipping charters and machine tool manufacturers worldwide.

top_event.headline: Supertanker Shipbuilding Revolution at Kure
top_event.wealth_driver: Daniel K. Ludwig leases the former Imperial Japanese Navy shipyards in Kure, Japan, constructing the world's first modern bulk carriers and supertankers.

top_event.headline: Getty Strikes Oil in Partitioned Neutral Zone
top_event.wealth_driver: After four years of exploration and $30M expended, Getty's Pacific Western Oil strikes massive commercial crude at Wafra Well No. 1.

top_event.headline: Neutral Zone Production Surge & Getty Takes Global #1
top_event.wealth_driver: Full-scale crude extraction at the Wafra concession lifts Getty Oil and Tidewater valuations, moving J. Paul Getty into a tie for global #1.

top_event.headline: Passing of Calouste Gulbenkian
top_event.wealth_driver: Oil pioneer Calouste 'Mr. Five Percent' Gulbenkian passes away, bequeathing his Iraqi oil stakes to charity; J. Paul Getty solidifies sole possession of the top spot.

top_event.headline: Suez Crisis Shipping Charter Windfall
top_event.wealth_driver: Closure of the Suez Canal forces oil shipments around Africa, multiplying charter day-rates for the independent supertanker fleets of Getty, Ludwig, and Onassis.

top_event.headline: Fortune Magazine Names Getty Richest Living American
top_event.wealth_driver: Fortune's landmark wealth investigation crowns J. Paul Getty as the wealthiest living American, estimating his oil and industrial empire at up to $1 billion.

top_event.headline: Sutton Place Acquisition & Global Corporate Governance
top_event.wealth_driver: Getty establishes operations at Sutton Place in England to oversee his 200 subsidiary corporations, expanding refining capacity across the North Atlantic.

top_event.headline: Getty Approaches Ten Figures Nominal
top_event.wealth_driver: Rapid downstream gasoline distribution across Western Europe pushes Getty's fortune to $950 million nominal ($10.92 billion CPI-adjusted).

top_event.headline: Passing of Rockefeller Jr. & Getty's Ascendancy
top_event.wealth_driver: John D. Rockefeller Jr. passes away in May, dispersing his remaining fortune into trusts; J. Paul Getty stands as the undisputed wealthiest private individual globally.

top_event.headline: Sarir Basin Discovery in Libya
top_event.wealth_driver: Nelson Bunker Hunt and H.L. Hunt discover the massive Sarir oil field in Cyrenaica, setting off an immense new stream of independent petroleum revenues.

top_event.headline: Kure Shipyard Giant Bulk Carriers
top_event.wealth_driver: Daniel K. Ludwig pioneers commercial bulk ore carriers exceeding 100,000 deadweight tons, narrowing the equity gap with Howard Hughes.

top_event.headline: Hughes Tool Monopolistic Dominance
top_event.wealth_driver: Hughes Tool Company's worldwide patent grip on rolling cone rock drill bits channels massive non-operating cash surpluses to Howard Hughes.

top_event.headline: Getty Oil North Sea Exploration
top_event.wealth_driver: Offshore petroleum exploration in the North Sea and expansion of Tidewater Oil refineries extend Getty's lead as the top global industrialist.

top_event.headline: Full Libyan Crude Extraction
top_event.wealth_driver: Pipeline completions connect the Sarir field to the Mediterranean coast, delivering hundred-thousand-barrel daily flows for Hunt and pushing his fortune toward ten figures.

top_event.headline: Hughes $546M TWA Stock Liquidation
top_event.wealth_driver: Howard Hughes is ordered by federal courts to divest his 75% stake in Trans World Airlines, receiving a single check for $546.5M cash—the largest single private transaction in history.

top_event.headline: Six-Day War Closes Suez & Passing of Krupp
top_event.wealth_driver: Indefinite closure of the Suez Canal triggers historic supertanker charter rates for Ludwig, Onassis, and Niarchos, while Alfried Krupp passes away, ending the family dynasty.

top_event.headline: Hughes Las Vegas Acquisition Spree
top_event.wealth_driver: Operating from his Desert Inn suite, Howard Hughes deploys liquid TWA cash to buy out iconic Las Vegas casinos, hotels, airports, and thousands of mining claims.

top_event.headline: Ludwig Launches the Jari Project
top_event.wealth_driver: Daniel K. Ludwig pours hundreds of millions into the Amazon basin, purchasing 4 million acres for silviculture, bauxite mining, and a floating pulp mill.

top_event.headline: North Sea Oil Discoveries & Supertanker Fleets
top_event.wealth_driver: Offshore exploration in the North Sea and booming global tanker transport consolidate J. Paul Getty's grip on the world's largest private fortune.

top_event.headline: Nixon Closes the Gold Window
top_event.wealth_driver: The suspension of dollar-gold convertibility sparks a multi-year bull market in tangible assets, commodities, and independent petroleum reserves.

top_event.headline: Pre-Embargo Petroleum Accumulation
top_event.wealth_driver: Rising inflation and tightening global refinery capacity lift market values across Getty Oil subsidiaries and privately held bulk transport fleets.

top_event.headline: First OPEC Oil Shock & Hunt Silver Accumulation
top_event.wealth_driver: The Arab oil embargo quadruples crude prices, causing independent producers to boom while Nelson Bunker Hunt begins aggressive physical silver forward buying.

top_event.headline: Passing of H.L. Hunt & Peak Oil Margins
top_event.wealth_driver: Texas oil patriarch H.L. Hunt passes away, dividing his vast empire among heirs, while J. Paul Getty's energy empire hits record cash profits.

top_event.headline: Passing of Aristotle Onassis
top_event.wealth_driver: Shipping icon Aristotle Onassis passes away in France; Getty maintains #1 as North Sea crude brings initial pipeline deliveries ashore.

top_event.headline: Passing of Hughes & Getty; Ludwig Takes the Crown
top_event.wealth_driver: Howard Hughes dies in April and J. Paul Getty dies in June, propelling reclusive shipping, mining, and real estate titan Daniel K. Ludwig to global #1.

top_event.headline: Amazon Basin Industrialization & Hunt Silver Syndicate
top_event.wealth_driver: Ludwig's multi-million-acre Jari estate expands into commercial forestry, while Bunker Hunt partners with Arab financiers to absorb major Comex silver contracts.

top_event.headline: The Great Silver Squeeze Escalates
top_event.wealth_driver: Rapidly accumulating over 40 million ounces of physical bullion and aggressive paper long contracts propels Nelson Bunker Hunt past Daniel K. Ludwig to global #1.

top_event.headline: Second Oil Crisis & Epic Silver Parabola
top_event.wealth_driver: Iranian revolution disruptions double oil prices while spot silver catapults from $6 to over $25/ounce, making Bunker Hunt the wealthiest private person on Earth.

top_event.headline: Silver Thursday Collapse & Ludwig Reclaims #1
top_event.wealth_driver: The Hunt brothers' leveraged corner on the physical silver market unravels as Comex margin rules change, restoring shipping and real estate magnate Daniel K. Ludwig to global #1.

top_event.headline: Tokyo Asset Acceleration
top_event.wealth_driver: Rapid appreciation in Tokyo commercial land values and Seibu Railway real estate holdings pushes Yoshiaki Tsutsumi past Ludwig into the global lead.

top_event.headline: Inaugural Forbes 400 Wealth Survey
top_event.wealth_driver: Forbes publishes its first comprehensive American wealth list naming Ludwig #1 in the US ($2.0B), while Tsutsumi's unlisted Seibu land holdings anchor global #1 ($4.5B).

top_event.headline: Getty Oil Takeover Battle Commences
top_event.wealth_driver: Rising acquisition bids for Getty Oil shares elevate Gordon Getty's trust valuation, while Tsutsumi's Seibu Group accelerates resort and hotel construction across Japan.

top_event.headline: Texaco Acquires Getty Oil for $10.1B
top_event.wealth_driver: Texaco's massive buyout of Getty Oil unlocks liquidity for Gordon Getty, while Tsutsumi's unlisted land assets surge alongside Tokyo's soaring real estate market.

top_event.headline: The Plaza Accord & Yen Currency Surge
top_event.wealth_driver: The G5 Plaza Accord triggers rapid yen appreciation against the US dollar, instantly expanding the dollar-denominated valuations of Japanese real estate titans.

top_event.headline: Tokyo Real Estate Hyper-Inflation
top_event.wealth_driver: Commercial land prices in central Tokyo soar by more than 50% in a single year, elevating Tsutsumi and Mori's property empires to global dominance.

top_event.headline: Inaugural Forbes World's Billionaires Ranking
top_event.wealth_driver: Forbes officially publishes its first international billionaires issue, confirming Yoshiaki Tsutsumi ($20B) and Taikichiro Mori ($15B) as the world's richest private individuals.

top_event.headline: Peak Japanese Bubble Dominance
top_event.wealth_driver: Japanese real estate and Nikkei equities achieve historic peaks, granting Japanese property and railway developers six of the top ten global wealth spots.

top_event.headline: Nikkei All-Time High at 38,915
top_event.wealth_driver: On the final trading day of the decade, the Tokyo Stock Exchange peaks at 38,915, anchoring Tsutsumi and Mori at the pinnacle of private global wealth.

top_event.headline: Tokyo Real Estate Peak & Japanese Hegemony
top_event.wealth_driver: Extreme commercial real estate valuations in central Tokyo anchor Japanese railway, leisure, and office tower magnates at the summit of private global fortunes.

top_event.headline: Walmart Retail Explosion Across America
top_event.wealth_driver: Rapid nationwide supercenter rollout and proprietary satellite logistics send Walmart equity soaring, pushing Sam Walton to the #1 global spot ahead of Japan's asset deflation.

top_event.headline: Passing of Sam Walton & Tokyo Office Resilience
top_event.wealth_driver: Following Sam Walton's passing in April and the division of his estate among heirs, Mori Building patriarch Taikichiro Mori ascends to global #1 on central Tokyo commercial lease cashflows.

top_event.headline: Passing of Taikichiro Mori & Windows 3.1 Surge
top_event.wealth_driver: Taikichiro Mori passes away in January; Tsutsumi regains the individual top spot while Bill Gates rapidly advances as Windows 3.1 sells over a million copies per month.

top_event.headline: PC Enterprise Shift Narrowing the Gap
top_event.wealth_driver: Japanese property asset values continue to contract post-bubble, allowing software equity gains to close the margin on Tsutsumi's remaining real estate lead.

top_event.headline: Launch of Windows 95 & Gates Takes the Crown
top_event.wealth_driver: Commercial launch of Windows 95 creates unprecedented demand for personal computer operating systems, establishing Bill Gates as the undisputed richest individual on Earth.

top_event.headline: Internet Browser Wars & Hong Kong Property Surge
top_event.wealth_driver: Microsoft's bundled software dominance accelerates equity gains, while Henderson Land Development pushes Hong Kong developer Lee Shau-kee to the global #3 spot.

top_event.headline: Dot-Com Inception & Asian Financial Crisis
top_event.wealth_driver: The onset of the Asian Financial Crisis pressures regional property moguls, while soaring US tech and Berkshire Hathaway equities widen the gap at the top.

top_event.headline: Microsoft Crosses $50 Billion Mark
top_event.wealth_driver: Exploding consumer internet adoption and PC workstation installations push Bill Gates past $50 billion nominal, while Paul Allen surges into the global top 3.

top_event.headline: Peak Dot-Com Euphoria & The Centibillionaire Threshold
top_event.wealth_driver: On the height of the dot-com boom, Microsoft equity valuation pushes Bill Gates to an intraday peak above $100 billion, closing the century with unprecedented private wealth concentration.

top_event.headline: Dot-Com Crash & Enterprise Tech Resilience
top_event.wealth_driver: Despite the initial dot-com equity plunge deflating speculative tech valuations, Bill Gates and Larry Ellison retain the top spots globally on enterprise software cash flows.

top_event.headline: Tech Retrenchment & Value Investing Rebound
top_event.wealth_driver: Continued deflation in internet equities erodes founder holdings, while Warren Buffett's Berkshire Hathaway recovers strongly to reclaim the global #2 rank.

top_event.headline: Post-Bubble Market Trough & European Retail Expansion
top_event.wealth_driver: As broader stock markets hit post-dot-com lows, non-cyclical European retail giants like Karl Albrecht's Aldi discount empire expand their market share across the continent.

top_event.headline: Global Equity Trough & Latin American Telecom Rise
top_event.wealth_driver: Equity markets bottom globally following geopolitical conflicts; Carlos Slim's consolidation of América Móvil establishes the telecom base for his decade-long ascent.

top_event.headline: Economic Rebound & Walton Family Consolidation
top_event.wealth_driver: Consumer spending surges lift Walmart revenues past $250 billion, placing five Walton family members firmly inside the global top ten.

top_event.headline: Commodity Supercycle & Mittal's Global Steel Empire
top_event.wealth_driver: Rapid industrialization in developing markets accelerates global demand for raw materials; Lakshmi Mittal's cross-border steel mergers propel him to global #3.

top_event.headline: European Luxury & IKEA Retail Expansion
top_event.wealth_driver: Expanding global consumer purchasing power lifts Ingvar Kamprad's IKEA retail footprint and Bernard Arnault's LVMH luxury empire into the international top ten.

top_event.headline: Macau Gaming Expansion & Telecom Surge
top_event.wealth_driver: Sheldon Adelson's Sands Macao and Venetian expansion sparks a massive casino IPO rally, while Carlos Slim closes the gap with Gates and Buffett.

top_event.headline: Buffett Takes #1 & Indian Tycoons Surge
top_event.wealth_driver: Warren Buffett unseats Bill Gates after a 13-year reign, while India places four industrialists (Mittal, Ambani brothers, K.P. Singh) inside the global top eight.

top_event.headline: Great Recession Trough & Capital Contraction
top_event.wealth_driver: The global financial crisis wipes hundreds of billions from worldwide billionaire balance sheets; Gates reclaims #1 as software shares prove more resilient than heavy cyclicals.

top_event.headline: Carlos Slim Overtakes Bill Gates
top_event.wealth_driver: Rapid wireless telecommunications penetration across Latin America via América Móvil pushes Mexican telecom magnate Carlos Slim to global #1, ending 15 years of US dominance.

top_event.headline: América Móvil Consolidation & Post-Crisis Peak
top_event.wealth_driver: A 19% rise in the Mexican stock market, currency strengthening, and the full consolidation of América Móvil expand Carlos Slim's fortune by $20.5 billion in twelve months.

top_event.headline: European Fast Fashion & Retail Expansion
top_event.wealth_driver: Rapid store expansion by Inditex (Zara) and Swedish retailer H&M lifts Amancio Ortega and Stefan Persson, while Carlos Slim retains #1 for the third consecutive year.

top_event.headline: Amancio Ortega Reaches Global Top 3
top_event.wealth_driver: Inditex stock surges on aggressive international e-commerce and retail expansion, propelling Zara founder Amancio Ortega past Warren Buffett to global #3.

top_event.headline: Bill Gates Reclaims World's Richest Title
top_event.wealth_driver: A strong rally in Microsoft shares combined with diversified gains in Canadian National Railway and Ecolab via Cascade Investment returns Gates to global #1.

top_event.headline: Gates Peaks at $79.2B & Buffett Reaches $72.7B
top_event.wealth_driver: Sustained US equity strength expands corporate valuations; Warren Buffett gains $14.5B on Berkshire Hathaway operations while Gates retains the top spot.

top_event.headline: Bezos & Zuckerberg Enter Global Top 10
top_event.wealth_driver: Rapid cloud computing and mobile ad monetization drive Amazon and Facebook valuations higher, lifting Jeff Bezos and Mark Zuckerberg into the global top six.

top_event.headline: Amazon Web Services Expansion & Tech Acceleration
top_event.wealth_driver: Surging cloud enterprise infrastructure adoption expands tech multiples, pushing Jeff Bezos to $72.8B to contest Gates and Buffett for leadership.

top_event.headline: Jeff Bezos Becomes Modern History's First $100B+ Billionaire
top_event.wealth_driver: Amazon's stock surges more than 80% in twelve months, making Jeff Bezos the first person in Forbes tracking history to surpass $100 billion nominal on the annual list.

top_event.headline: Amazon Extends Dominance & Arnault Reaches $76B
top_event.wealth_driver: Amazon reaches record logistics scale, cementing Bezos at $131B, while Bernard Arnault's LVMH acquires Christian Dior and expands luxury margins globally.

top_event.headline: E-Commerce Surge During Global Lockdowns
top_event.wealth_driver: As the global pandemic drives consumer retail online, Amazon equity surges, cementing Jeff Bezos as the world's richest person for the third straight year.

top_event.headline: Stimulus Liquidity Boom & Tesla's Parabolic Run
top_event.wealth_driver: Historic monetary expansion accelerates valuations across enterprise tech and electric vehicles, lifting Jeff Bezos to $177B while Elon Musk ascends to global #2.

top_event.headline: Tesla $1 Trillion Valuation & Musk Captures #1
top_event.wealth_driver: Rapid EV production scaling and record operating margins push Tesla past a $1 trillion market cap, making Elon Musk the world's richest person at $219 billion.

top_event.headline: European Luxury Overtakes Tech Contraction
top_event.wealth_driver: Rising interest rates compress US tech equity multiples while resilient global demand for Louis Vuitton and Christian Dior lifts Bernard Arnault to #1 at $211 billion.

top_event.headline: Record LVMH Revenue & Generative AI Inception
top_event.wealth_driver: LVMH posts record global luxury earnings to keep Bernard Arnault at the world's apex at $233 billion, as cloud compute and AI hardware begin lifting Silicon Valley multiples.

top_event.headline: AI Infrastructure Boom & Musk Reclaims Top Spot
top_event.wealth_driver: Rapid advancements in autonomous driving, commercial robotics, and xAI's infrastructure propel Elon Musk back to #1 at $342B, while Zuckerberg jumps to #2 on open AI adoption.

top_event.headline: SpaceX IPO & The Trillion-Dollar Frontier
top_event.wealth_driver: The public listing of SpaceX alongside Tesla's commercial autonomous fleet rollout cements Elon Musk at an unprecedented $839B baseline, leading a top tier dominated by frontier compute architects.
